questions.question: In 1928, who discovered that when a ray of coloured light enters a liquid, a fraction of the light scattered by that liquid is of a different colour?
questions.questionHtml: In 1928, who discovered that when a ray of coloured light enters a liquid, a fraction of the light scattered by that liquid is of a different colour?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is CV Raman.

Key Points

  • Sir Chandrasekhara Venkata Raman, discovered on 28 February 1928, that when a beam of coloured light entered a liquid, a fraction of the light scattered was of a different color, dependent on material property.
  • This radiation effect of molecular scattering of light bears the name of ‘Raman Effect’, from which many applications in photonic communications and spectroscopy evolved.
  • The Raman Effect is the process of scattering light particles by molecules of a medium.
  • The scattering occurs due to a change in the wavelength of light as it enters the medium.
  • When a beam of light travels through a dust-free, transparent chemical, a small fraction of the light emerges in directions other than where it should.
  • Light consists of particles called photons, whose energy is directly proportional to the frequency with which they travel. 
  • When they strike molecules in a medium at high speeds, they bounce back and scatter in different directions depending on the angle with which they hit the molecules.

Additional Information

  • Lord Rayleigh’s first researches were mainly mathematical, concerning optics and vibrating systems, but his later work ranged over almost the whole field of physics, covering sound, wave theory, colour vision, electrodynamics, electromagnetism, light scattering, the flow of liquids, hydrodynamics, the density of gases, viscosity, capillarity, elasticity, and photography. 
  • Satyendra Nath Bose FRS was an Indian mathematician and physicist specializing in theoretical physics.
  • He is best known for his work on quantum mechanics in the early 1920s, in developing the foundation for Bose statistics and the theory of the Bose condensate.
  • John Tyndall FRS was a prominent 19th-century Irish physicist.
  • His initial scientific fame arose in the 1850s from his study of diamagnetism.

questions.question: ‘Beri-Beri’ is caused by the deficiency of __________.
questions.questionHtml: ‘Beri-Beri’ is caused by the deficiency of __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is thiamine.

Key Points

  • Thiamine:
    • Thiamine, also known as Vitamin B1, is essential for energy metabolism and nerve function.
    • A deficiency of thiamine leads to Beri-Beri.
    • Beri-Beri can manifest in various forms, including wet Beri-Beri (affecting the cardiovascular system) and dry Beri-Beri (affecting the nervous system).
    • Symptoms include muscle weakness, fatigue, and neurological problems.
    • Thiamine is found in foods like whole grains, legumes, and pork.

Additional Information

  • Riboflavin:
    • Riboflavin, or Vitamin B2, is important for cell growth and energy production.
    • A deficiency of riboflavin can cause conditions like cheilosis (cracked lips) and glossitis (inflamed tongue).
    • It is vital for healthy skin and eyes.
    • It is found in dairy products, eggs, and leafy green vegetables.
    • It also helps with the metabolism of fats.
  • Cyanocobalamin:
    • Cyanocobalamin, or Vitamin B12, is crucial for red blood cell formation and nerve function.
    • A deficiency of Vitamin B12 can lead to anemia and neurological problems.
    • It is primarily found in animal products like meat, fish, and dairy.
    • It is essential for DNA synthesis.
    • Vegetarians and vegans may need to supplement their diet with B12.
  • Niacin:
    • Niacin, or Vitamin B3, is involved in energy metabolism and DNA repair.
    • A deficiency of niacin causes Pellagra, which is characterized by dermatitis, diarrhea, and dementia.
    • It is important for healthy skin and the nervous system.
    • Niacin is found in foods like meat, poultry, and grains.
    • It can also be produced by the body from the amino acid tryptophan

questions.question: The Israel Institute of Technology has developed a concept named after the Indian mathematician ______
questions.questionHtml: The Israel Institute of Technology has developed a concept named after the Indian mathematician ______
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Ramanujan.

Key Points

  • Israel Institute of Technology has developed a concept, which is called as ‘Ramanujan machine’ after one of the great Indian mathematicians Srinivasa Ramanujan. 
  • The Ramanujan Machine is a novel way to do mathematics by harnessing your computer power to make new discoveries, it generates conjectures (mathematical statements that are proposed as true statements) for fundamental constants.
  • Srinivasa Ramanujan was born on 22 Dec 1887, and his birth anniversary is celebrated as National Mathematics Day in his memory.
    • Notable works - Landau–Ramanujan constant, Mock theta functions, Ramanujan conjecture, Ramanujan prime, Ramanujan–Soldner constant, Ramanujan theta function, Ramanujan's sum, Rogers–Ramanujan identities, Ramanujan's master theorem, Ramanujan–Sato series.

Additional Information

  • Aryabhata was supposed to be the first Indian mathematician and astronomer of ancient India.
    • He is well known for his invention of the digit "0". 
    • His other notable works are Aryabhaṭiya, Arya-Siddhanta, Explanation of lunar eclipse and solar eclipse, rotation of Earth on its axis, a reflection of light by moon, sinusoidal functions, solution of single-variable quadratic equation, the value of π correct to 4 decimal places, the diameter of Earth.
  • Bhaskaracharya was an Indian mathematician and astronomer. 
    • His notable works are  Siddhanta-Siromani and Karaṇa Kautuhala, 
    • He is well known for his discovery of the principles of differential calculus and its application to astronomical problems and computations.
    • In the honor of Bhaskaracharya on 20 November 1981, ISRO launched the Bhaskara II satellite.
  • Dattatreya Ramchandra Kaprekar was an Indian recreational mathematician.
    • He had described several classes of natural numbers including the Kaprekar, Harshad, and self numbers, and discovered the Kaprekar's constant,

questions.question: Which physicist is known to establish the relationship between mechanical work and heat transfer?
questions.questionHtml: Which physicist is known to establish the relationship between mechanical work and heat transfer?
questions.solution: James Prescott Joule is renowned for establishing the relationship between mechanical work and heat transfer, leading to the first law of thermodynamics. His experiments showed that heat and mechanical work are interchangeable, forming the basis for the principle of conservation of energy, which states that energy cannot be created or destroyed, only converted from one form to another. The unit of energy, the joule (J), is named in his honor. Joule's work significantly advanced the Industrial Revolution by providing a scientific basis for the efficient use of energy in engines and machinery.

questions.question: Which format of email address is correct?
questions.questionHtml: Which format of email address is correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is xyz@website.co.in.

Key Points

The general format of an email address is localpart@domain.

For example jsmith@example.com.

3 Parts of an Email Address

  • Username:
    • The first part of an email address is the username.
    • This is the unique name that you or your ISP select.
  • @ Symbol: 
    • ​An “at” or “@” symbol is the second part of an email address.
    • This fits in between the username and the domain of your email address.
    • When you insert the symbol, your email program recognizes the character and sends the email to the domain name that follows it.
  • Domain:
    • The last part of an email address is the domain, which can be broken down into two portions: the mail server and the top-level domain.
    • The mail server is the server hosting the email account.
    • For example, Yahoo email accounts use “yahoo” as the server name, while Gmail uses “Gmail” as the server name.
    • The top-level domain is the extension, such as .com, .net or .info.

questions.question: Who among the following physicists invented the voltaic pile, the forerunner of the modern battery, in 1800?
questions.questionHtml: Who among the following physicists invented the voltaic pile, the forerunner of the modern battery, in 1800?
questions.solution: Alessandro Volta, an Italian physicist, invented the voltaic pile in 1800, the precursor to the modern battery. This was the first electrical battery that could provide a continuous electric current, a significant advancement in electromagnetism and electrochemistry. The voltaic pile consisted of alternating zinc and copper discs with saltwater-soaked cardboard between them. Volta's contributions also include the discovery of methane and laying the groundwork for electrochemistry. The unit of electric potential, the volt, is named after him. He was a long-time professor at the University of Pavia, and his invention led to numerous scientific and practical advancements in electricity.

questions.question: Which web portal was launched by the Department of Telecommunications for sharing information on mobile towers and EMF emission compliance?
questions.questionHtml: Which web portal was launched by the Department of Telecommunications for sharing information on mobile towers and EMF emission compliance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Tarang Sanchar.

Key Points

  • Tarang Sanchar is a web portal launched by the Department of Telecommunications (DoT).
  • The portal aims to provide information about mobile towers and their compliance with Electromagnetic Field (EMF) emission norms.
  • It offers a user-friendly interface for the public to get detailed information on EMF emissions from mobile towers in their vicinity.
  • The initiative is part of the government's efforts to address public concerns regarding the health hazards due to EMF emissions from mobile towers.

Additional Information

  • Electromagnetic Field (EMF) Emissions
    • EMF emissions are produced by mobile towers and other electronic devices.
    • There are concerns about the potential health risks associated with long-term exposure to EMF emissions.
    • The Department of Telecommunications (DoT) has set stringent norms for EMF emissions to ensure they are within safe limits.
  • Department of Telecommunications (DoT)
    • The DoT is a department of the Ministry of Communications of the executive branch of the Government of India.
    • It is responsible for formulating developmental policies for the accelerated growth of the telecommunication services in the country.
    • The DoT also enforces wireless regulatory measures, monitors the performance of licensees, and promotes private investment in the telecommunications sector.
  • Mobile Towers
    • Mobile towers are structures that support antennas and other communication equipment for cellular networks.
    • They play a critical role in providing mobile network coverage and connectivity.
    • Proper placement and regulation of mobile towers are essential to ensure efficient network performance and public safety.
  • Public Health and Safety
    • Public health and safety are major considerations in the regulation of EMF emissions from mobile towers.
    • The government has implemented various measures to address public concerns and ensure that EMF emissions remain within safe limits.
    • Initiatives like the Tarang Sanchar portal help increase transparency and public awareness regarding EMF emissions and mobile tower compliance.

questions.question: In 1820, who found that electric current causes a nearby magnetic needle to move and thus discovered electromagnetism?
questions.questionHtml: In 1820, who found that electric current causes a nearby magnetic needle to move and thus discovered electromagnetism?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Hans Christian Oersted.

Key Points
  • Hans Christian Oersted began a new scientific epoch when he discovered that electricity and magnetism are linked.
  • He showed by experiment that an electric current flowing through a wire could move a nearby magnet.
  • Hans Christian Oersted was a Danish physicist and chemist born on August 14, 1777 – died on Mach 09, 1851. 
  • Oersted is still known today for Oersted's Law, electric current, electromagnetism, piperine discovery, and finally formulation of metallic aluminum.​

Additional Information

  • One of the leading figures of early American history, Benjamin Franklin (1706-1790) was a statesman, author, publisher, scientist, inventor, and diplomat. Benjamin Franklin was many things in his lifetime: a printer, a postmaster, an ambassador, an author, a scientist, and a Founding Father. Above all, he was an inventor, creating solutions to common problems, innovating new technology, and even making life a little more musical.
  • James Clerk Maxwell is most famous for his theory of electromagnetism, which showed that light was electromagnetic radiation. His theory is considered to have paved the way for both quantum mechanics and Einstein's theory of special relativity.
  • Andre-Marie Ampere the astatic needle, a critical component of the modern astatic galvanometer, and was the first to demonstrate that a magnetic field is generated when two parallel wires are charged with electricity. He is generally credited as one of the first to discover electromagnetism.

  • Jupiter has overall 79 satellites out of which 26 are yet to be named.

questions.question: Planetary scientists call the thin gaseous envelope around the Moon as the _______.
questions.questionHtml: Planetary scientists call the thin gaseous envelope around the Moon as the _______.
questions.solution:
• Planetary scientists prefer to call the thin gaseous envelope around the Moon as the ‘Lunar exosphere’.
  • Here, molecules in the air are so few and far between, they rarely come into contact with one another. 
  • Still, the gases found around the Moon do have important effects on conditions near the surface. 
  • While the Earth’s atmosphere near the mean sea level contains ~1019 atoms per cubic centimetre of volume, the lunar exosphere contains ~ 104 to 106 atoms per cubic centimetre.
  • Argon-40 (40 Ar), which is one of the isotopes of the noble gas Argon, is an important constituent of the lunar exosphere. 
  • It originates from the radioactive disintegration of Potassium-40 (40 K), which has a half-life of ~1.2 X 109 years.

questions.question: Which of the following is the Galilean moon that was observed in 1610 by the Italian astronomer Galileo Galilei using a homemade telescope?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is the Galilean moon that was observed in 1610 by the Italian astronomer Galileo Galilei using a homemade telescope?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Ganymede.

Key Points

  • Ganymede, a satellite of Jupiter, is the largest and most massive of the Solar System's moons. 
  • The ninth-largest object in the Solar System, it is the largest without a substantial atmosphere.​

Additional Information

  • Phobos is the innermost and larger of the two natural satellites of Mars, the other being Deimos. 
    • Both moons were discovered in 1877 by American astronomer Asaph Hall. Phobos is named after the Greek deity Phobos, a son of Ares and twin brother of Deimo.
  • Titan is the largest moon of Saturn and the second-largest natural satellite in the Solar System.
    • It is the only moon known to have a dense atmosphere and is the only known object in space other than Earth on which clear evidence of stable bodies of surface liquid has been found.
  • Namaka is the smaller, inner moon of the trans-Neptunian dwarf planet Haumea.
    • It is named after Nāmaka, the goddess of the sea in Hawaiian mythology and one of the daughters of Haumea.

questions.question: For what discovery is Evangelista Torricelli famous?
questions.questionHtml: For what discovery is Evangelista Torricelli famous?
questions.solution: Evangelista Torricelli, an Italian physicist and mathematician, is famous for his invention of the mercury barometer. He was a student of Galileo and also made advances in optics and the method of indivisibles. The Torr unit is named after him. Torricelli was born on 15 October 1608 and died on 25 October 1647.

questions.question: Which is the joint digital skills initiative for employability through digital skills by National Career Service and Microsoft India?
questions.questionHtml: Which is the joint digital skills initiative for employability through digital skills by National Career Service and Microsoft India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Digisaksham.

Key Points

  • Digisaksham is a joint initiative by the National Career Service (NCS) and Microsoft India.
  • The program aims to enhance employability by providing digital skills training to the youth.
  • It includes training in various digital skills, such as data analysis, coding, and software development.
  • The initiative is targeted at job seekers registered on the NCS portal, helping them improve their job prospects.

Additional Information

  • National Career Service (NCS)
    • The National Career Service is an initiative by the Ministry of Labour and Employment, Government of India.
    • It aims to bridge the gap between job seekers and employers by providing a unified platform for career-related services.
    • NCS offers services like job matching, career counseling, vocational guidance, and information on skill development courses.
    • The portal caters to all stakeholders in the employment ecosystem, including job seekers, employers, training providers, and placement organizations.
  • Microsoft India
    • Microsoft India is a subsidiary of Microsoft Corporation, a global technology company.
    • It focuses on empowering every individual and organization in India to achieve more through digital transformation.
    • Microsoft India offers a wide range of products and services, including software, cloud computing, and AI solutions.
    • The company is committed to driving digital skills development and fostering innovation in the country.
  • Digital Skills
    • Digital skills refer to the ability to use digital devices, communication applications, and networks to access and manage information.
    • These skills include basic computer literacy, internet navigation, data analysis, coding, and software development.
    • Proficiency in digital skills is essential for individuals to participate effectively in the digital economy and the modern workforce.
    • Continuous learning and upskilling in digital technologies are crucial for career advancement and employability in various industries.

questions.question: Which is an advanced weather satellite of India configured with improved imaging system and atmospheric sounder?
questions.questionHtml: Which is an advanced weather satellite of India configured with improved imaging system and atmospheric sounder?
questions.solution: INSAT-3D is an advanced Indian weather satellite with an improved imaging system and atmospheric sounder, launched by ISRO on 26th July 2013 from the Guiana Space Centre. It features a 6-channel imager and a 19-channel sounder for detailed atmospheric data, enhancing meteorological observations and data relay. INSAT-3D is crucial for weather forecasting, disaster warning, and search and rescue operations, significantly improving prediction accuracy for agriculture, aviation, and maritime sectors. Part of the INSAT series, it supports telecommunications, broadcasting, meteorology, and rescue operations, with data utilized by the India Meteorological Department and disaster management agencies.

questions.question: ______ is concerned with constructing records of past climates and climatic events by analysis of tree growth characteristics, especially growth rings.
questions.questionHtml: ______ is concerned with constructing records of past climates and climatic events by analysis of tree growth characteristics, especially growth rings.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Dendroclimatology

Key Points

  • Dendroclimatology is concerned with constructing records of past climates and climatic events by analysis of tree growth characteristics, especially growth rings.
    • It is the analysis of tree ring growth patterns to determine past climate variations.

Additional Information

  • Bioclimatology (biometeorology) is the study of the relationships between climate (weather) and living organisms.
  • Historical climatology is the study of historical changes in climate and their effect on civilization from the emergence of homininis to the present day.
  • Climatology is the study of climate and how it changes over time.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is/are correct? I- Radio broadcasting started in India in 1923 by the Radio Club of Bombay. II- All India Radio came into being in 1936. III - In 1976, TV was delinked from All India Radio (AIR) and got a separate identity as Door darshan (DD).
questions.questionHtml:
Which of the following statements is/are correct?

I- Radio broadcasting started in India in 1923 by the Radio Club of Bombay.

II- All India Radio came into being in 1936.

III - In 1976, TV was delinked from All India Radio (AIR) and got a separate identity as Door darshan (DD).

options.text: Both I and II are correct.
options.html: Both I and II are correct.

options.text: I, II and III are correct
options.html: I, II and III are correct

options.text: Both II and III are correct.
options.html: Both II and III are correct.

questions.solution: Radio broadcasting in India began in 1923 with the Radio Club of Bombay. All India Radio (AIR) was established in 1936, taking over from the Indian State Broadcasting Service. In 1976, television broadcasting was separated from AIR and became an independent entity known as Doordarshan (DD). Therefore, the statements that radio broadcasting started in 1923, AIR was established in 1936, and TV was delinked from AIR in 1976 to become Doordarshan are all correct.

questions.question: Which of the following is/are primary device/devices of storage? I. Cache II. RAM III. Hard drive
questions.questionHtml:
Which of the following is/are primary device/devices of storage?

I. Cache

II. RAM

III. Hard drive
questions.solution:
Cache memory:

  • A cache is a hardware or software component that stores data so future requests for that data can be served faster.
  • It is a small-sized type of volatile computer memory that provides high-speed data access to a processor and stores frequently used computer programs, applications and data.

Random Access Memory (RAM):

  • Random Access Memory is volatile. That means data is retained in RAM as long as the computer is on, but it is lost when the computer is turned off.
  • When the computer is rebooted, the OS and other files are reloaded into RAM, usually from an HDD or SSD.

Hard drive:

  • A hard disk drive (HDD), hard disk, hard drive, or fixed disk, is an electro-mechanical data storage device that stores and retrieves digital data using magnetic storage with one or more rigid rapidly rotating platters coated with magnetic material.
